rationale: The candidate reads as a stepped, twisting mass with some sectional ambition, but the four views do not resolve into one coherent neighborhood-living gesture. The silhouette is mostly an arbitrary tiered pyramid rather than a capacity-bearing or program-legible section, and the mass appears over-determined by stacking rather than by a clear ground threshold or public void. The blue access edge is acknowledged only weakly: there is no convincing court, notch, or undercut that engages the frontage as a public entry condition. In top/oblique views the solid also feels like it compresses and turns without a stable anchor, so repair integrity is limited. It does resonate loosely with terraced neighborhood precedents, but not enough to overcome the weak program expression. Program-fit fails because a neighborhood building here needs an active ground edge plus a usable void or terrace; this form currently behaves more like a generic sculpted stepped block than a street-responsive mixed-use mass.
